<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Chairman&#146;s Letter</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Dear Shareholder,</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>During 2006, a year in which Vanguard 500 Index Fund marked its 30th anniversary, the fund returned 15.6% for Investor Shares and 15.7% for Admiral Shares. The fund outperformed the average return of its peers, and met its objective of closely tracking its unmanaged benchmark, the Standard &amp; Poor&#146;s 500 Index. Despite its strong return, the fund made no capital gains distributions, a benefit to shareholders in taxable accounts. </font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Shareholders who own the fund in a taxable account may wish to review the report on the fund&#146;s after-tax returns on page 26.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>On September 29, Vanguard introduced Signal Shares for the fund, which are available to certain qualifying institutional investors. Those shares returned 6.7% for the three months since their inception.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Strong second half pushed stocks to new high</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Beginning in mid-July, stocks climbed steadily through the remainder of the year, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average setting a record high on December 27. For the year, the broad U.S. stock market gained 15.9%. Despite a soft housing sector and ongoing troubles within the U.S. auto industry, the economy continued to grow and corporate profits remained strong.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For the year, small-capitalization stocks beat out large-cap issues, and value stocks outperformed their growth-oriented counterparts. International stocks continued to best domestic equities, particularly in </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>emerging markets and Europe. A declining dollar further enhanced returns abroad for U.S.-based investors.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Bond returns remained modest as the Fed paused its rate hikes</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The Federal Reserve Board extended its money-tightening campaign during the first half of the year, raising its target for the federal funds rate four times. The Fed then paused, leaving the target rate unchanged at 5.25% for the rest of the year, and inflation fears eased. Bond yields declined in the second half of the year, and short-term yields were higher than longer-term yields.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Fixed income returns for 2006 were modest, with the broad taxable bond market returning 4.3%, and municipal bonds providing 4.8%.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Fund benefited from advances across all industry groups</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For Vanguard 500 Index Fund, and indeed the broader stock market, 2006 was a story in two parts. In the first half of the year, the benchmark S&amp;P 500 Index posted a tepid 2.7% return, as jittery investors feared the economy was overheating. Inflation concerns then moderated in mid-summer, and the market gained momentum. A strong second half propelled the S&amp;P 500 Index to a 15.8% 12-month return, which the 500 Index Fund closely tracked. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The index experienced broad-based gains, as all ten of its industry sectors recorded positive returns for the year. Through a combination of their strong returns and their weightings in the index, the financials, energy, and consumer discretionary</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>sectors were the largest contributors to the index&#146;s overall result. Within the financials sector (which returned 19.1%), investment banks and brokerage firms were standouts, particularly in the final few months of the year. Energy stocks (up 24.2%) fluctuated during the period as did oil and gas prices, but delivered impressive returns for yet another year. Consumer discretionary stocks returned 18.8%, despite weakness in the homebuilding category, as several large media firms rebounded from underwhelming results in 2005. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Smaller sectors also packed a punch. Telecommunication services, utilities, and materials (whose weightings, if combined, would still rank as one of the index&#146;s smallest sectors) all outperformed the index&#146;s overall result. Investors in telecom stocks reacted favorably to consolidation in the sector,  while electric, gas, and diversified utilities firms turned in impressive gains. In materials, chemical stocks did well, and the index&#146;s steel companies rose an average of 80% during the 12 months.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Two of the economy&#146;s less-flashy segments&#151;industrials and consumer staples&#151;posted solid double-digit returns that slightly trailed the index&#146;s overall result. Meanwhile, information technology and health care, which returned 8.3% and 7.6%, respectively, were the laggards in 2006. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Fund has outperformed many of its actively managed peers</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Over the past decade, the Investor Shares of the 500 Index Fund registered an average annual return of 8.3%, outpacing the average result of competing funds (most of which are actively managed) by 1.6 percentage points. <p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>competitors is the result of its lower operating and transaction costs and the fund&#146;s full investment in the market without the drag of a cash holding&#151;an enduring advantage. In addition, the fund nearly matched the return of its unmanaged benchmark, which has no costs or operating expenses. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Managing a portfolio that simply &#147;owns the market&#148; isn&#146;t nearly as simple as it might sound. In seeking to track the returns of the S&amp;P 500 Index, your fund&#146;s advisor&#151;Vanguard Quantitative Equity Group&#151;must, in essence, hit a moving target every day that the stock market is open. By combining its collective experience and skill with sophisticated trading strategies, the Quantitative Equity Group has hit the mark consistently for more than three decades. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The group&#146;s task is made easier by Vanguard&#146;s low expenses. The 500 Index Fund is offered at a fraction of the cost of most of its peers. This allows for tighter tracking of the target index, and ultimately enables a greater portion of the fund&#146;s returns to reach shareholders&#146; pockets. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Thirty years later, fund&#146;s strategy remains simple, but powerful</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>In the 30 years since its inception, the case for Vanguard 500 Index Fund has grown stronger with every year of testing in the real-world laboratory of the financial markets. While the 500 Index Fund story remains the same&#151;low costs, diversified exposure to 500 of the U.S. market&#146;s largest stocks&#151;the investment environment has changed substantially. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For example, the universe of mutual funds for investors to choose from has grown from several hundred in 1976 to many thousand today. Such an immense array of choices can make selecting the appropriate funds seem overwhelming for individual investors. In addition, today&#146;s investors are barraged with much more &#147;noise&#148;&#151;newspapers, magazines, cable networks, websites, and blogs&#151;each happy to opine on which stocks and which funds will outperform the market. Amid all the chatter, &#147;seeking to match the market&#146;s return&#148; does not make a good sound bite. Indexing isn&#146;t a fancy investment strategy&#151;perhaps it&#146;s even a bit dull. But it has proven to be a smart and powerful approach. From its 1976 inception through December 31, 2006, the 500 Index Fund&#146;s 12.2% average annual return has translated nearly all of the stock market&#146;s gains into shareholder wealth.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>After 30-plus years, we still believe the 500 Index Fund is a strong foundation for a balanced and diversified investment portfolio. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Notes to Financial Statements</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard 500 Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, and Signal Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria. Signal Shares are designed for institutional investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, and account-size criteria. Signal Shares were first issued on September 29, 2006.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>A.</font></B><font size=2> The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid
prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets. </font></i><font size=2>Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets </font></i><font size=2>as an asset (liability) and in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Operations </font></i><font size=2>as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>5. Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;'><font size=2>21</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>6. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>B.</font></B><font size=2> The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2006, the fund had contributed capital of $7,047,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 7.04% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>C.</font></B><font size=2> Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the year ended December 31, 2006, the fund realized $344,693,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2006, the fund had $15,978,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had available realized losses of $6,571,975,000 to offset future net capital gains of $193,358,000 through December 31, 2008, $890,248,000 through December 31, 2009, $3,087,963,000 through December 31, 2010, $145,498,000 through December 31, 2011, $44,874,000 through December 31, 2012, $757,853,000 through December 31, 2013, $1,156,454,000 through December 31, 2014, and $295,727,000 through December 31, 2015.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>At December 31, 2006, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was $72,264,866,000. Net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $46,885,577,000, consisting of unrealized gains of $51,548,019,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and $4,662,442,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</font></p>

FIN 48 will be effective for the fund&#146;s fiscal year ending December 31, 2007. Management is in the process of analyzing the fund&#146;s tax positions for purposes of implementing FIN 48; based on the analysis completed to date, management does not believe the adoption of FIN 48 will result in any material impact to the fund&#146;s financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>To the Trustees of Vanguard Index Funds and Shareholders of Vanguard 500 Index Fund:</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>In our opinion, the accompanying statement of net assets and the related statements of operations and of changes in net assets and the financial highlights present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Vanguard 500 Index Fund (one of the funds constituting Vanguard Index Funds, hereafter referred to as the &#147;Fund&#148;) at December 31, 2006, the results of its operations for the year then ended, the changes in its net assets for each of the two years in the period then ended and the financial highlights for each of the periods indicated, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. These financial statements and financial highlights (hereafter referred to as &#147;financial statements&#148;) are the responsibility of the Fund&#146;s management; our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits.
We conducted our audits of these financial statements in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits, which included confirmation of securities at December 31, 2006 by correspondence with the custodian and broker and by agreement to the underlying ownership records for the Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Your Fund&#146;s After-Tax Returns</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>This table presents returns for your fund both before and after taxes. The after-tax returns are shown in two ways: (1) assuming that an investor owned the fund during the entire period and paid taxes on the fund&#146;s distributions, and (2) assuming that an investor paid taxes on the fund&#146;s distributions </font><i><font size=2>and </font></i><font size=2>sold all shares at the end of each period.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Calculations are based on the highest individual federal income tax and capital gains tax rates in effect at the times of the distributions and the hypothetical sales. State and local taxes were not considered. After-tax returns reflect any qualified dividend income. (In the example, returns after the sale of fund shares may be higher than those assuming no sale. This occurs when the sale would have produced a capital loss. The calculation assumes that the investor received a tax deduction for the loss.)</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The table shows returns for Investor Shares only; returns for other share classes will differ. Please note that your actual after-tax returns will depend on your tax situation and may differ from those shown. Also note that if you own the fund in a tax-deferred account, such as an individual retirement account or a 401(k) plan, this information does not apply to you. Such accounts are not subject to current taxes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>About Your Fund&#146;s Expenses</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The table below illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways: </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>&#149; Based on actual fund return.</font></b><font size=2> This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#147;Ending Account Value&#148; shown is derived from the fund&#146;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#147;Expenses Paid During Period.&#148; </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>&#149; Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return.</font></b><font size=2> This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#146;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;'><font size=2>28</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Glossary </font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Beta.</font></b><font size=2> A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Earnings Growth Rate.</font></b><font size=2> The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Expense Ratio.</font></b><font size=2> The percentage of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Foreign Holdings.</font></b><font size=2> The percentage of a fund represented by stocks or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><b><font size=2>Inception Date.</font></b><font size=2> The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#146;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Median Market Cap.</font></b><font size=2> An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Price/Book Ratio.</font></b><font size=2> The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Price/Earnings Ratio.</font></b><font size=2> The ratio of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#146;s future growth.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>R-Squared.</font></b><font size=2> A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Return on Equity.</font></b><font size=2> The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Short-Term Reserves.</font></b><font size=2> The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Turnover Rate.</font></b><font size=2> An indication of the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Yield.</font></b><font size=2> A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield, expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income provided by securities in the index.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:center;'><font size=2>29</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>The People Who Govern Your Fund</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The trustees of your mutual fund are there to see that the fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part owner of the fund. Your fund&#146;s trustees also serve on the board of directors of The Vanguard Group, Inc., which is owned by the Vanguard funds and provides services to them on an at-cost basis.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>A majority of Vanguard&#146;s board members are independent, meaning that they have no affiliation with Vanguard or the funds they oversee, apart from the sizable personal investments they have made as private individuals. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Our independent board members bring distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public service to their task of working with Vanguard officers to establish the policies and oversee the activities of the funds. Among board members&#146; responsibilities are selecting investment advisors for the funds; monitoring fund operations, performance, and costs; reviewing contracts; nominating and selecting new trustees/directors; and electing Vanguard officers. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each trustee serves a fund until its termination; or until the trustee&#146;s retirement, resignation, or death; or otherwise as specified in the fund&#146;s organizational documents. Any trustee may be removed at a shareholders&#146; meeting by a vote representing two-thirds of the net asset value of all shares of the fund together with shares of other Vanguard funds organized within the same trust. The table on these two pages shows information for each trustee and executive officer of the fund. The mailing address of the trustees and officers is P.O. Box 876, Valley Forge, PA 19482.  </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.83%; text-indent:-2.83%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>&#62;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the 2006 fiscal year, the Investor Shares of the three Vanguard small-capitalization index funds produced returns ranging from 11.9% to 19.2%.</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.83%; text-indent:-2.83%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.83%; text-indent:-2.83%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>&#62;&nbsp;&nbsp;All of the funds closely tracked their benchmark indexes, and all outperformed their peer groups&#146; average returns.</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.83%; text-indent:-2.83%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.83%; text-indent:-2.83%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>&#62;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the small-cap arena, value stocks outpaced growth issues, and the financials and industrials sectors performed particularly well.</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.83%; text-indent:-2.83%;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=3>Chairman&#146;s Letter</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Dear Shareholder,</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>For the fiscal year ended December 31, all three Vanguard Small-Cap Index Funds tracked their indexes with precision and delivered healthy returns. In the small-capitalization arena, value-oriented stocks outperformed their growth counterparts by a considerable margin. The returns for all three Vanguard funds were superior to the average returns produced by their peers.</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For taxable investors, it&#146;s worth noting that the benefits of holding index funds can be even greater, as the funds&#146; low turnover and Vanguard&#146;s disciplined management generally limit the distribution of realized capital gains. During 2006, none of the small-cap index funds distributed a capital gain. (For a report on the funds&#146; after-tax returns, see page 60.) </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Strong second half pushed stocks to new high</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Beginning in mid-July, stocks climbed steadily through the remainder of the year, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average setting a record high on December 27. For the year, the broad U.S. stock market gained 15.9%. Despite a soft housing sector and ongoing troubles within the U.S. auto industry, the economy continued to grow and corporate profits remained strong.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For the year, small-capitalization stocks beat out large-cap issues, and value stocks outperformed their growth-oriented counterparts. International stocks continued</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=1>2</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>to best domestic equities, particularly in emerging markets and Europe. A declining dollar further enhanced returns abroad for U.S.-based investors.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Bond returns remained modest as the Fed paused its rate hikes</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The Federal Reserve Board extended its money-tightening campaign during the first half of the year, raising its target for the federal funds rate four times. The Fed then paused, leaving the target rate unchanged at 5.25% for the rest of the year, and inflation fears eased. Bond yields declined in the second half of the year, and short-term yields were higher than longer-term yields.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Fixed income returns for 2006 were modest, with the broad taxable bond market returning 4.3% and municipal bonds providing 4.8%.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>2006 was a healthy year for small-cap stocks</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>In a robust market environment for stocks, small-cap stocks performed very well over the past 12 months. The Investor Shares of the Vanguard small-cap index funds produced returns ranging from 19.2% for the Small-Cap Value Index Fund to 11.9% for the Small-Cap Growth Index Fund. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>The Small-Cap Index Fund, which combines the holdings of the two other funds, returned 15.6%. Results for all three funds were</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- EEDocs PBEnd-->

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>superior to the average returns produced by their peer groups, which are largely actively managed funds.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard Quantitative Equity Group, which oversees the funds, once again succeeded in making sure each one closely tracked the performance of its target index. These results are a tribute to the adept portfolio-construction and trading methodologies continuously refined by the group. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The performance of the three funds reflected their respective weightings in the market&#146;s different industry sectors. For example, the Small-Cap Value Fund had about 37% of its assets in financial stocks, which experienced healthy gains, particularly for banks and real estate investment trusts. In contrast, the Small-Cap Growth Fund had a sizable exposure (22% of assets) to the information technology sector, which produced more modest returns. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.15pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each of the three funds held a different double-digit weighting in the industrials sector, which performed particularly well in 2006. There were detractors among the sectors as well, particularly the struggling homebuilding industry within the consumer discretionary sector, where poor performance dragged on returns for each of the funds. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Long-term returns show the value of indexing </font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Indexing is a long-term strategy, and over time the benefits of its market-matching approach become clear. While there will inevitably be years when the funds&#146; actively managed competitors perform better, it&#146;s</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>no surprise when index funds outperform their competition, as each of the three small-cap index funds did in 2006.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The table below shows how the three funds have performed over the longer term in comparison with their competitors and target benchmarks. The table also shows what would have become of a hypothetical $10,000 initial investment in each fund&#146;s Investor Shares. The Small-Cap Index Fund, for example, returned an average of 10.0% a year, which would have transformed the $10,000 initial investment into $25,993. The Small-Cap Growth and Value Index Funds are &#147;younger&#148;&#151;they were opened in 1998&#151;and the 2000&#150;2002 bear market therefore figures more prominently in their long-term performance. Since inception, average annual returns for these two funds have been 8.1% and 10.2%, respectively. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The table also shows that two of the funds trailed the average returns of their peer groups. That is largely because, until 2003, the funds tracked indexes that did not reflect the small-cap stock market as it is viewed by active investment managers. Since May 2003, the funds have targeted indexes from Morgan Stanley Capital International that better represent the market from an active investment standpoint. We believe that, in the future, differences between the returns of these index funds and the average results of their actively managed competitors should depend more </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><b><font size=2>Investors need perspective and a balanced strategy</font></b></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>In 2006, all of the Vanguard small-cap index funds outperformed their peer-group averages. While this 12-month performance is gratifying, we generally counsel investors that neither under- nor outperformance is all that meaningful in the short term. In fact, we always encourage Vanguard shareholders to evaluate their investments from a long-term perspective. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Sticking with a carefully considered, balanced portfolio of stock, bond, and money market mutual funds suited to your unique circumstances can be key to your long-term investing success.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:11.5pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>As an investor, you can weather the market&#146;s uncertainties by holding to a well-planned strategy. We believe that investing in Vanguard&#146;s small-cap index funds is a smart way to capitalize on this important segment of the total stock market. </font></p>

For the first and third fiscal quarters, the fund files the lists with the SEC on Form N-Q. Shareholders can look up the fund&#146;s Forms N-Q on the SEC&#146;s website. Forms N-Q may also be reviewed and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room (see the back cover of this report for further information).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:22.95pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:58.5%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:18.6pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=2>Notes to Financial Statements</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers five classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Signal Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria. Signal Shares are designed for institutional investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, and account-size criteria. Signal Shares were first issued on December 15, 2006. Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. ETF Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>A.</font></B><font size=2> The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid
prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets</font></i><font size=2>. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets </font></i><font size=2>as an asset (liability) and in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Operations </font></i><font size=2>as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:84%;text-align:left;'><font size=1>23</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:22.95pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>5. Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:2.2pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>6. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:2.2pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:2.2pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>B.</font></B><font size=2> The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2006, the fund had contributed capital of $1,355,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 1.35% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:2.2pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>C.</font></B><font size=2> Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:2.2pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the year ended December 31, 2006, the fund realized $694,982,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:2.2pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2006, the fund had $2,188,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had available realized losses of $402,458,000 to offset future net capital gains of $326,341,000 through December 31, 2011, and $76,117,000 through December 31, 2015.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:2.2pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>At December 31, 2006, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was $10,619,573,000. Net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $3,686,107,000, consisting of unrealized gains of $4,137,633,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and $451,526,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>G.</font></B><font size=2> In June 2006, the Financial Accounting Standards Board issued Interpretation No. 48 (&#147;FIN 48&#148;), &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes". FIN 48 establishes the minimum threshold for recognizing, and a system for measuring, the benefits of tax-return positions in financial statements. FIN 48 will be effective for the fund&#146;s fiscal year ending December 31, 2007. Management is in the process of analyzing the fund&#146;s tax positions for purposes of implementing FIN 48; based on the analysis completed to date, management does not believe the adoption of FIN 48 will result in any material impact to the fund&#146;s financial statements.</font></p>

Note, too, that both investment returns and principal value can fluctuate widely, so an investor&#146;s shares, when sold, could be worth more or less than their original cost.</font></b><font size=2> The returns shown do not reflect taxes that a shareholder would pay on fund distributions or on the sale of fund shares.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:22.95pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:18.6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:left;'><font color="#FF0000"><b><font size=3>Notes to Financial Statements</font></b></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Institutional Shares, and ETF Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. ETF Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>A.</font></B><font size=2> The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:left;'><font size=2>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued
using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:left;'><font size=2>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets. </font></i><font size=2>Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Net Assets </font></i><font size=2>as an asset (liability) and in the </font><i><font size=2>Statement of Operations </font></i><font size=2>as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:justify;'><font size=2>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:2.33%;text-align:left;'><font size=2>4. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=1>38</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>
<!-- EEDocs PBStart-->
<HR noshade align="center" width="100%" size="2">
<p style='page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- EEDocs PBEnd-->

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'>
</p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:52.33%;text-align:right;'><font color="#FF0000"><font size=1>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund</font></font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-left:52.33%;text-align:left;'><font size=2>&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>5. Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>6. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>B.</font></B><font size=2> The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2006, the fund had contributed capital of $289,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 0.29% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>C.</font></B><font size=2> Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>During the year ended December 31, 2006, the fund realized $151,028,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2006, the fund had $184,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had available realized losses of $59,847,000 to offset future net capital gains of $13,814,000 through December 31, 2011, $15,893,000 through December 31, 2014, and $30,140,000 through December 31, 2015.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>At December 31, 2006, the cost of investment securities for tax purposes was $2,571,162,000. Net unrealized appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $513,860,000, consisting of unrealized gains of $610,361,000 on securities that had risen in value since their purchase and $96,501,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since their purchase.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><B><font SIZE=2>E.</font></B><font size=2> The market value of securities on loan to broker-dealers at December 31, 2006, was $100,172,000, for which the fund received cash collateral of $106,145,000.</font></p>

In June 2006, the Financial Accounting Standards Board issued Interpretation No. 48 (&#147;FIN 48&#148;), &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes.&#148; FIN 48 establishes the minimum threshold for recognizing, and a system for measuring, the benefits of tax-return positions in financial statements. <p style=' margin-bottom:3.7pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>This Statement summarizes the fund&#146;s holdings by asset type (common stocks, bonds, etc.) and by industry sector. Details are reported for each of the fund&#146;s 50 largest individual holdings and for investments that, in total for any issuer, represent more than 1% of the fund&#146;s net assets. The total value of smaller holdings is reported as a single amount within each category. </font></p>

<p style=' margin-bottom:0pt; margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;'><font size=2>The fund provides a complete list of its holdings four times in each fiscal year, at the quarter-ends. For the second and fourth fiscal quarters, the complete listing of the fund&#146;s holdings is available electronically on Vanguard.com and on the Securities and Exchange Commission&#146;s website (www.sec.gov), or you can have it mailed to you without charge by calling 800-662-7447. For the first and third fiscal quarters, the fund files the lists with the SEC on Form N-Q. Shareholders can look up the fund&#146;s Forms N-Q on the SEC&#146;s website. Forms N-Q may also be reviewed and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room (see the back cover of this report for further information).</font></p>
